categories: ["การตั้งครรภ์"]
conventional_description:
Retained products of conception (RPOC) refers to fetal or placental tissue that remains in the uterus after a miscarriage, stillbirth, or delivery. It is typically diagnosed by ultrasound and presents with symptoms such as prolonged bleeding, pelvic pain, fever, or an open cervical os.
Conventional management generally falls into three categories: expectant management (waiting for the body to expel the tissue naturally), medical management using medications like misoprostol to stimulate uterine contractions, or surgical evacuation via dilation and curettage (D&C). The choice depends on the amount of retained tissue, the severity of bleeding, and the patient's clinical stability.
conventional_treatments: Standard treatment includes expectant management for incomplete miscarriages with minimal symptoms, medical management with prostaglandins like misoprostol to induce uterine contractions, and surgical evacuation via suction curettage when bleeding is heavy or infection is suspected. Antibiotics may be prescribed if there are signs of endometritis. The goal is complete evacuation to prevent complications such as hemorrhage, infection, and intrauterine adhesions.
tcm_understanding:
In TCM, retained products of conception are understood as a failure of the uterus to properly expel its contents - but the reason for that failure can be completely different from one person to the next. The uterus relies on a steady supply of Qi to push and Blood to nourish. When either is lacking, or when something blocks the passage, the deceased tissue cannot descend.
The Spleen and Stomach are the engines of Qi and Blood production. When they are weak - often from poor diet, overwork, or constitutional deficiency - the uterus simply doesn't have the fuel it needs to contract and expel the tissue. This is the pattern of Qi and Blood Deficiency: the body is too exhausted to push.
But sometimes the problem isn't a lack of energy - it's a blockage. Physical trauma, intense emotional strain, or cold congealing the blood can create Blood Stagnation in the uterine vessels. The passage is locked shut by dark, clotted blood. Or emotional turmoil - anger, resentment, grief - can cause Liver Qi to stagnate and generate Heat, which scorches the blood and creates a sticky, hot obstruction. And when the Spleen is weak and Dampness accumulates, Cold-Dampness can gum up the uterine passages like thick mud, freezing the Qi mechanism and trapping the tissue.
This is why TCM doesn't treat all retained tissue the same way. The exhausted mother needs nourishment and gentle support. The mother with stabbing pain and dark clots needs blood moved and stasis broken. The angry, flushed mother with fresh red bleeding needs heat cleared. And the mother with cold, heavy pain and sticky discharge needs Dampness dried and the uterus warmed. Each pattern points to a completely different treatment - which is why pattern differentiation matters.
tcm_diagnosis:
A TCM practitioner begins by listening carefully to the quality of the pain and the nature of any discharge. Dull, lingering discomfort with pale watery bleeding and a sense of emptiness points toward Qi and Blood Deficiency - the uterus simply lacks the energy to expel the retained tissue. This pattern often shows up in a person who looks pale and exhausted, with a thin white tongue coat and a weak, thready pulse.
When the pain is sharp, fixed, and stabbing, with dark purple clots and a choppy pulse, the practitioner suspects Blood Stagnation. This pattern often follows physical trauma or intense emotional strain. The tongue body may appear purplish with dark spots, and the person usually describes the pain as severe and cramping rather than dull.
If the person reports fresh red bleeding alongside a red tongue, a wiry rapid pulse, and signs of irritability or chest fullness, the practitioner considers Liver Qi Stagnation transforming into Heat. Here emotional upset has generated heat that scorches the blood, creating a mixed picture of stagnation and heat signs.
Damp-Cold presents differently again: the pain feels cold and heavy rather than sharp, and the discharge is sticky and yellowish rather than dark. The tongue coat is thick and white, and the pulse feels slow and slippery. This pattern tells the practitioner that the Spleen is failing to transform fluids properly, allowing dampness to combine with cold and obstruct the uterus.

patterns.symptoms: ["Dull lower abdominal pain or cold sensation", "Pale pink or light red vaginal discharge", "Fatigue and shortness of breath", "Pale or sallow complexion", "Dizziness and heart palpitations", "Poor appetite and spontaneous sweating"]
patterns.worse_with: Physical exertion, Poor nutrition or cold foods, Emotional stress and worry
patterns.better_with: Absolute bed rest, Warm nourishing soups and congee, Calm quiet environment
patterns.why_this_happens: In this pattern, the mother's Qi and Blood are deeply depleted. Qi provides the pushing force and Blood provides the material foundation for the uterus to function. When both are severely lacking, the uterus lacks the energy to contract and expel the deceased fetus. Think of it like a pump that has lost its power - without sufficient Qi to drive it and sufficient Blood to nourish the uterine muscles, the dead tissue simply cannot be pushed out, leading to retention with dull, lingering pain.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: pale body, may be thin or have teeth marks on the edges, thin white coating. Pulse: fine, weak, and forceless, especially in the right Guan position.
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: This pattern is defined by a profound lack of Qi and Blood, so any activity or poor nutrition depletes these resources further. Rest and nourishing foods directly rebuild the body's reserves, providing the Spleen with the raw materials to generate Qi and Blood. A calm environment prevents emotional strain from further damaging the Spleen's digestive function. Once Qi and Blood are replenished, the uterus regains the strength to contract and expel the deceased fetus.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Focus on easily digestible, warm, nourishing foods like congee with lean protein, bone broth, and dark leafy greens. Avoid cold, raw, and greasy foods that weaken Spleen Qi. Absolute rest is essential to conserve Qi and allow the body's resources to focus on recovery.

patterns.symptoms: ["Severe stabbing uterine pain", "Dark purple vaginal discharge with clots", "Pain worsens with pressure and at night", "Dusky facial complexion and lips"]
patterns.worse_with: Cold food and drinks, Emotional stress and frustration, Prolonged sitting or lying without movement, Cold environment
patterns.better_with: Warm compress on the lower abdomen, Gentle movement and walking, Emotional calm and low stress
patterns.why_this_happens: When trauma, emotional constraint, or cold congeals the blood, the uterine vessels become blocked. This trapped blood creates a physical obstruction that prevents the deceased fetus from descending. The stabbing pain and dark clots are direct signs of this blood stasis locking the uterus shut.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: dark purple body with stasis spots, distended dark sublingual veins. Pulse: choppy (涩 sè), rough and uneven like a knife scraping bamboo.
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: Cold causes blood to congeal, which is the root of this pattern, so warmth and movement provide direct relief. Emotional stress causes Liver Qi stagnation, which further blocks Qi flow and prevents the blood from moving. Gentle movement helps Qi flow, but overexertion drains Qi and worsens the stasis.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Avoid cold and raw foods that congeal blood. Gentle walking can help move Qi and blood, but avoid strenuous activity. Keep the abdomen warm with a hot water bottle to promote circulation.

patterns.pattern_name: Liver Qi Stagnation that transforms into Heat
patterns.symptoms: ["Irritability and explosive anger", "Bitter taste in the mouth", "Distending or burning rib-side pain", "Fresh red vaginal bleeding", "Restlessness and disturbed sleep"]
patterns.worse_with: Emotional stress and frustration, Spicy and fried foods, Alcohol
patterns.better_with: Emotional release, Cooling foods, Gentle stretching
patterns.why_this_happens: When emotional distress like anger or resentment is held in over time, the Liver's job of keeping Qi moving smoothly gets blocked. That stuck Qi then generates heat, which rises to cause bitter taste, a red face, and irritability. The heat scorches the blood and creates stasis in the uterus, trapping the deceased fetus and preventing its delivery.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: red body, redder at the sides, with a yellow coating. Pulse: wiry and rapid (弦数 xián shuò), forceful at the left Guan position.
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: Emotional upset causes Liver Qi to stagnate, which is the root of this pattern's heat and stasis. Spicy, greasy foods and alcohol add external heat to an already heated condition. Cooling foods and emotional release help unblock the Qi, allowing heat to naturally dissipate and blood stasis to be resolved.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Prioritize emotional release through gentle movement like walking or talking to a trusted friend. Eat cooling, bitter greens like celery and romaine, and avoid spicy, fried, or greasy foods that add heat.

patterns.symptoms: ["Cold aching lower abdominal pain", "Sticky yellowish vaginal discharge", "Heavy sensation in body and limbs", "Bland taste in the mouth and no thirst", "Loose stools or diarrhoea"]
patterns.worse_with: Cold and damp weather, Raw or cold foods, Dairy and greasy food
patterns.better_with: Warmth on the abdomen, Light cooked foods, Dry warm environment
patterns.why_this_happens: When the Spleen is weak, it cannot properly transform fluids, leading to internal Dampness. When this Dampness combines with a pathogenic Cold lodged in the uterus, it becomes a thick, obstructive sludge. This Cold-Dampness gums up the uterine passages and freezes the Qi mechanism, so the deceased fetus is trapped in a cold, stagnant environment and cannot be expelled.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: Pale, swollen, teeth-marked body with a thick white greasy coating, excessively moist. Pulse: Deep, slow, and slippery or soggy.
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: Cold and raw foods directly add to the pathological Cold and Dampness, making the obstruction thicker and heavier. Warmth and dry heat help to thaw the Cold and evaporate the Dampness, which unblocks the Qi mechanism and allows the Spleen to regain its transporting function.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Keep the low abdomen warm with a hot water bottle and avoid raw, cold, or greasy foods that tax the Spleen and create more Dampness. Small amounts of warm, cooked ginger tea may help dispel the internal cold.

formulas.translation: Eight Treasure Decoction · Míng dynasty, 1529 CE
formulas.properties: Warm, Tonifies Qi, Nourishes Blood, Strengthens the Spleen
formulas.description: A classical formula that simultaneously replenishes both Qi and Blood, created by combining two famous prescriptions: Si Jun Zi Tang (for Qi) and Si Wu Tang (for Blood). It is commonly used for people who feel chronically tired, look pale or sallow, have a poor appetite, experience dizziness or heart palpitations, and feel generally run down due to dual deficiency of Qi and Blood.

formulas.translation: Cinnamon Twig and Poria Pill · Eastern Hàn dynasty, ~200 CE
formulas.properties: Slightly Warm, Invigorates Blood and Dispels Stasis, Disperses Fixed Masses, Warms the Channels and Disperses Cold
formulas.description: A classical formula that gently promotes blood circulation and dissolves masses in the lower abdomen. Originally used for gynecological conditions caused by blood stasis, it is now widely applied for conditions like uterine fibroids, ovarian cysts, painful periods, and endometriosis. Its mild but steady action makes it suitable for long-term use.

formulas.translation: Peach Pit and Carthamus Four-Substance Decoction · Yuán dynasty, ~1291 CE
formulas.properties: Warm, Invigorates Blood and Dispels Stasis, Nourishes Blood, Regulates menstruation
formulas.description: A classical formula that both nourishes and invigorates the Blood, used to address menstrual irregularities, period pain, and other conditions caused by Blood stagnation combined with Blood deficiency. It builds on the famous Si Wu Tang (Four-Substance Decoction) by adding Peach Kernel and Safflower to strengthen its ability to move stagnant Blood and promote healthy circulation.

formulas.translation: Gentian Liver-Draining Decoction · Qīng dynasty, 1682 CE
formulas.properties: Cold, Drains excess Fire from the Liver and Gallbladder, Clears Damp-Heat from the Lower Burner, Clears Heat from the Liver channel
formulas.description: A powerful cooling formula used to address conditions caused by excess heat and dampness in the Liver and Gallbladder systems. It is commonly used for red, painful eyes, headaches, ear problems, irritability, urinary difficulties, and skin conditions like shingles, particularly when accompanied by a bitter taste in the mouth, dark urine, and a feeling of heat or inflammation along the sides of the body or in the genital area.

formulas.translation: Calm the Stomach Powder · Sòng dynasty, ~1051 CE
formulas.properties: Warm, Dries Dampness, Strengthens the Spleen, Moves Qi
formulas.description: A foundational formula for resolving dampness that has accumulated in the digestive system. It is used when dampness obstructs the Spleen and Stomach, causing bloating, loss of appetite, nausea, a bland taste in the mouth, heavy limbs, fatigue, and loose stools. It works by drying dampness, restoring the Spleen's digestive function, and promoting the smooth flow of Qi in the abdomen.

faqs.question: Can TCM alone expel retained tissue after a miscarriage?
faqs.answer: Yes, in many cases TCM can effectively promote expulsion of retained tissue - but it depends entirely on the pattern. Qi and Blood Deficiency patterns require first building the mother's strength before the tissue can be safely expelled, which may take 1-2 weeks of herbal treatment. Blood Stagnation patterns often respond more quickly, sometimes within days. However, TCM should only be used under professional supervision, and any signs of heavy bleeding or infection require immediate conventional medical attention.

faqs.question: Is it safe to combine TCM herbal formulas with misoprostol or other medications?
faqs.answer: Combining TCM herbs with conventional medications like misoprostol should only be done under the guidance of both your TCM practitioner and your medical doctor. Some blood-moving herbs like Dang Gui (当归) and Yi Mu Cao (益母草) can amplify the effects of prostaglandins, potentially causing excessive bleeding. Always inform both practitioners of all medications and supplements you are taking.

faqs.question: How long does TCM treatment take to work for retained tissue?
faqs.answer: Timelines vary by pattern. Blood Stagnation often responds within days of starting herbs. Qi and Blood Deficiency typically requires 2-4 weeks - the body needs time to rebuild its strength before it can push out the tissue. Damp-Cold and Liver Qi Stagnation patterns fall somewhere in between. Your TCM practitioner will monitor your progress closely and adjust the formula as your condition changes.

faqs.question: Will acupuncture help with the pain from retained tissue?
faqs.answer: Yes. Acupuncture can help relieve the cramping and pain associated with retained tissue, especially when Blood Stagnation is the primary pattern. Points like Hegu (LI-4) and Sanyinjiao (SP-6) are commonly used to promote uterine contractions and move blood. For deficiency patterns, points like Zusanli (ST-36) and Guanyuan (REN-4) are used to gently build Qi and Blood while supporting the uterus. Pain relief from acupuncture can be immediate, though the underlying condition requires ongoing herbal treatment.

faqs.question: What should I eat while undergoing TCM treatment for retained tissue?
faqs.answer: Warm, cooked foods are essential - soups, congee, stews, and steamed vegetables. Avoid all raw, cold foods and icy drinks, which constrict the uterus and worsen stagnation. Dark leafy greens, small amounts of organ meats, and red dates (hong zao, 红枣) support Blood. Ginger and cinnamon can gently warm the uterus. Avoid spicy, greasy, and deep-fried foods, which create Dampness and Heat.

faqs.question: Can TCM prevent retained tissue in future pregnancies?
faqs.answer: By treating the underlying pattern that led to the retained tissue - whether that's building Qi and Blood, moving Blood Stagnation, or clearing Heat - TCM can help strengthen the constitution and reduce the risk of recurrence. This typically involves a course of herbal treatment and dietary therapy in the months following the loss, before attempting another pregnancy. Many TCM practitioners recommend waiting at least 3-6 months to rebuild fully.

research.title: 龍膽瀉肝湯合桂枝茯苓丸治療妊娠十週死胎不下醫案報告
research.description: A case report from Taiwan documenting the successful use of Long Dan Xie Gan Tang combined with Gui Zhi Fu Ling Wan to manage a retained dead fetus at ten weeks gestation. The patient presented with liver stagnation transforming into heat pattern, and the formula successfully induced expulsion of retained tissue without surgical intervention.
research.periodical: National Research Institute of Chinese Medicine, Taiwan. Case Report: Treatment of Retained Dead Fetus at Ten Weeks Gestation with Long Dan Xie Gan Tang and Gui Zhi Fu Ling Wan. 2016.
